newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bank investments, mergers on road to EMU.
newsitem.headline: Greek bank investments, mergers on road to EMU.

text.p: Investments in human and physical capital, mergers and acquisitions in the Greek banking sector will be part of the process towards the EMU, said the chairman of the National Bank of Greece, Theodore Karatzas.

"The course to EMU will be accompanied by investments in the production of banking goods and services, that is investments in human capital and technology, and mergers and acquisitions to the extent that operating expenses are cut or secure speedy growth and tolerable cost," said Karatzas.

The chairman of Greece's largest commercial bank was speaking on Greece and the EMU at a conference on the modernisation of the Greek banking system and capital markets organised by the Hellenic-American Chamber of Commerce and the Hellenic Bank Association.

Greek banks would enjoy the advantage of knowing the developing economies of the Balkans and the Middle East for about 10 years when the country enters into the EMU and this will differentiate them from other EU banks, said Karatzas.

"Our entry into the EMU will find Greek banks with at least 10 years of experience in these markets and a wide range of activities -- conventional financing for commerce, experience in mergers and acquisitions, leasing, direct investment financing and portfolio management," he said.
Developments in the banking sector will also strengthen the hand of local banks in the context of the EMU, said Karatzas.

"Our mission is just one, to see our future with confidence, to liberalise forces that we have but frequently ignore and go ahead," he said stressing that the banking sector's future has been shaped by the EU.
